record.original_question: Let H_k be the 2^k x 2^k Hadamard matrix from Sylvester's construction. For odd k, is the discrepancy equal to sqrt(2) * sqrt(2^k), i.e., disc(H_k) = sqrt(2) * sqrt(2^k)?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 13. Let Hk be the 2^k ×2^k Hadamard matrix obtained by the Sylvester construction (see above). For odd k, we have disc(Hk) = √2√(2^k).
Furthermore, Rares-Darius Buhai [Buh25] showed that Conjecture 13 is false by identifying a connection between discrepancy of Hk and a theory of non-linearity in Boolean Functions.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For an integer $k \ge 1$, define the Sylvester Hadamard matrix $H_k \in \{-1,+1\}^{2^k 	imes 2^k}$ recursively by $H_1 =  egin{pmatrix} 1 & 1 \ 1 & -1 \end{pmatrix}$ and $H_{k+1} =  egin{pmatrix} H_k & H_k \ H_k & -H_k \end{pmatrix}$. For an $n 	imes n$ real matrix $A$, define its discrepancy by
$$\operatorname{disc}(A) = \min_{x \in \{-1,+1\}^n} \|A x\|_\infty.$$
Determine whether the following identity holds for every odd positive integer $k$:
$$\operatorname{disc}(H_k) = \sqrt{2} \cdot \sqrt{2^k}.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture that disc(H_k) = sqrt(2)·sqrt(2^k) for odd k has been disproved by Rares-Darius Buhai, who established a connection between the discrepancy of the Sylvester Hadamard matrix and the theory of nonlinearity of Boolean functions, yielding counterexamples.

status_evidence.title: Discrepancy of Sylvester Hadamard matrices (Buhai)
status_evidence.snippet: Rares-Darius Buhai [Buh25] showed that Conjecture 13 is false by identifying a connection between discrepancy of Hk and a theory of non-linearity in Boolean Functions.
status_evidence.claim: The conjectured equality disc(H_k) = sqrt(2)·sqrt(2^k) for odd k is false.
